topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The tree is gone. I trace the edges of the stump, rough and jagged under my fingers, the air thick with the scent of fresh wood. This was more than just a tree; it was a witness, a silent guardian of my childhood, its branches marking the seasons of my life. Now, it’s just an empty space, a hollow reminder of what can vanish without a whisper. The yard feels different, smaller somehow, like the boundaries of my memories have been pushed back. I keep looking at the stump, expecting it to sprout again, to defy this silent erasure. But it’s just a stump, a final punctuation where there used to be a story.
